label: rejected

evidence.V1: Top view reads as a flagstone floor, but front, three-quarter and silhouette read as a plain thick slab with a faint row of bumps on top.
evidence.V2: Medium flagstones over a big base, but no small-scale detail (no chips, worn corners, grout depth variation); the base side is a large blank surface.
evidence.V3: Flagstones are uniform-height, near-identical rectangles in a grid - closer to stiff primitives than confident stylised stone (no tilt, rounding or size play).
evidence.V4: Flagstone tops carry a consistent chamfer that catches light, but the base slab edges look razor-sharp in the edge close-up.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups clean: no pinches, z-fighting or seams; 0 flipped faces, A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 3 values (dark, mid, light grey); sandstone and brick colourways keep the same disciplined 3-value structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material and stone hue fit the modular spec, but value distribution clusters (whole front row dark, centre light) and unchamfered base differ from the kit's chamfered made-object edges.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling passes (X IoU 0.987, Y 1.0).

evidence.V1: Reads as a flagstone floor block from top and three-quarter; silhouette shows the tile lips along the top edge, as expected for a floor module.
evidence.V2: Base slab (big), varied-size flagstones (medium), chamfered flagstone lips and joints (small).
evidence.V3: Stylised mixed-size flagstones with slight overhang lip; proportion suits a 2-stud floor module.
evidence.V4: Uniform chamfers on every flagstone catch the light in the flagstones and edge close-ups.
evidence.V5: Clean close-ups; cross_shell_overlaps 0, no seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values; dark tiles cluster along one edge but stay within a disciplined palette.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, chamfered stone: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass both axes.

evidence.V1: Top and three-quarter read as a flagstone floor, but front and silhouette are a plain 8x8x2 slab with a slightly overhanging bumpy lid, generic at 64 px from the side.
evidence.V2: Big (base slab) and medium (flagstones in mixed sizes and 3 values) are clear; no small tier (no chips, cracks, worn corners or grout detail) and the deep base sides are blank.
evidence.V3: Flagstones are uniform bevelled rectangles on a straight-sided box; mixed slab sizes help a little but the overall read is stiff and grid-regular.
evidence.V4: Close_flagstones and close_edge studio show even chamfers on every flagstone edge and corner catching a highlight; base slab edges carry a small consistent bevel.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean: flat stone tops, no pinches, seams or z-fighting; the small notches at joint corners in the flat close-up are where adjacent chamfers meet; A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light, mid, dark flagstones) with a dark base; sandstone and brick colourways keep the same value structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue, kit-range chamfers per wave-2 modular spec; matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes on X (iou 0.987) and Y (iou 1.0).

artifacts: value variation is clustered by region (dark front row and corners, light centre) so tiled copies will show a visible repeating band pattern
top_fixes: Scatter the three stone values randomly across tiles instead of in bands so tiling does not show a repeat
Give flagstones slight size, height and tilt variation plus a few chipped corners for small-scale detail
Chamfer the base slab edges and consider recessing/darkening it so the piece reads as floor, not a box
Distribute dark/light flagstones more evenly so tiled copies do not show a dark band
Add a subtle chamfer/inset line on the base slab sides
Optional small cracks or a missing-corner tile for character
Add a small tier: chipped corners, a crack or two, slight per-stone height/tilt variation
Break up the blank base sides (thinner slab or a visible mortar/bedding band) so the side view reads as flooring
Loosen the grid with more irregular flagstone sizes or offset joints for a more stylised read; tighten the X seam so tiling iou reaches 1.0
